rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 528.4, the best so far): the robot still leaves the line rather than oscillating. Oval finishes 11 of 20 (progress 0.94). The s-bend finishes 12 of 20 (progress 0.96). The slalom ends off track in all 20 runs at mean progress 0.42, with about 1.05 line-loss events per run and max_error around 0.064, above the 0.06 m limit. steering_oscillation is 0.23 to 0.39, well below the 0.5 warning level, so damping is not the limit. The step from speed 1.3 to 1.15 helped the s-bend (progress 0.79 to 0.96) but lowered oval completion (14 to 11 finishes), which suggests the speed is near a trade-off point. The slalom is the weakest track. Its alternating bends push the robot past the outer sensors, which lose the tape (about one loss per run), and then it drifts past the limit. Hypothesis (a) from iteration 4 points to wider sensor coverage. Changes: (1) Sensor spread widened from +/-0.035 m to +/-0.04 m, with spacing 0.02 m. This is still under the 0.025 m tape width, so the centre sensors keep overlapping coverage, and the edge sensors keep seeing tape at larger offsets, which should cut slalom line-loss events. (2) base_speed raised from 1.15 to 1.2, a compromise to recover oval finishes while keeping most of the s-bend gain. Oval time should stay well under 3 s. kp 5.0, kd 1.4, ki 0.01, sensor_size 0.016, mass 0.6, body and wheel geometry, sensor weights and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the wider spread can be read against iteration 4. Expected result: slalom line-loss events under 0.5 and slalom progress above 0.6, with oval and s-bend completion holding near iteration 4 levels. Hypotheses: (a) if slalom max_error still reaches 0.06 with line losses fixed, the limit is steering authority on the sharpest alternating bends, so kp should rise to about 5.5 with kd 1.5. (b) If oval completion falls below 0.5, base_speed should return to 1.15 and the slalom gain should come from geometry alone. (c) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.5, kd is too high relative to kp. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so the spread effect can be separated from the speed change.
